in_hebrew.name: סופיאנה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: על-פי הגרסה היוונית, סופיאנה (סופיה + אנה) יכולה להשמע כמילה המתארת נערה יפה, שבאה בעורף יופי.  השם נבחר כדי לסמל מישור, ולכן,  הגשמי והרוחני.  בעבר וביום הנוכחי,  השם עשוי להיחשב כשם המסמל יופי,  ופריחה.

in_greek.name: Σοφιάνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Σοφιάνα (Σοφία + Άνα) είναι το όνομα που αναφέρεται στην σοφία και την κρίση.  Ο Σοφιάνα ήταν το όνομα που έδωσαν στις πριγκίπισσες της Ρωμαϊκής Αυτοκρατορίας.  Στην κλασική εποχή,  ήταν το όνομα που έδωσαν σε γυναίκες που αρέσει την σοφία,  και την αγάπη.  Σήμερα,  το όνομα Σοφιάνα συνδέεται με την σοφία,  την πίστη και την ηρεμία.

in_latin.name: Sophiana
in_latin.long_meaning: Sophiana, forma pulchra, sapientia, est nomen quod significat formam pulchram, sapientia, et fides.  In antiqua aetas, Sophiana erat nomen quod impositum est puellis Romanorum Imperii.  Hodierna die, Sophiana connectio est formae pulchrae, sapientia, et fides.  In Ecclesia Christiana, Sophiana est nomen quod significat formam pulchram, sapientia, et fides.

in_english.name: Sophiana
in_english.long_meaning: Sophiana is a name that means beautiful form, wisdom, and gentle.  It is derived from the Greek words 'Sophia', meaning wisdom, and 'Anna', meaning gentle.  In the Bible, Sophia is the name of a female figure who represents wisdom.  In the early Christian church, Sophiana was a popular name among women who valued wisdom, beauty, and gentleness.  Today, Sophiana is a name that symbolizes intelligence, creativity, and compassion.

historical_references.reference: In Greek mythology, Sophia or Wisdom was one of the personifications of the goddesses of wisdom. The ancient Greeks believed that Sophia was the mother of all the goddesses and goddesses, and that she was the embodiment of divine wisdom. This belief in Sophia as a deity was prevalent during the Hellenistic period, from around 300 BC to 146 BC.

During the Early Christian period, the name Sophia came to be associated with the divine feminine and the Holy Spirit. The term 'Sophia' appears in various early Christian texts, such as the 'Gospel of the Hebrews' and the 'Gospel of Thomas', and is often depicted as a feminine figure who represents divine wisdom and is a manifestation of God. This belief in Sophia as a divine feminine figure was prevalent during the 2nd to 4th centuries AD.
historical_references.time_period: Early Christian Period (2nd to 4th centuries AD)
